answer: Verifiable delay functions curb Sybil attacks by forcing agents to evaluate non-parallelizable hash chains seeded by a public beacon. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of dedicating continuous single-core processor time per identity, preventing hardware multiplexing. Whether an agent tracks sable populations or negotiates trades, it must submit proofs within a fixed epoch delta. However, adversaries with overclocked custom silicon can compute chains faster to sustain multiple personas.
